item.title: Atari Hotels has officially broken ground in Phoenix, Arizona, with construction planned to complete in late 2028 to early 2029 for what could be the US’s next premier esports venue.
item.description:
Atari Hotels has officially broken ground in Phoenix, Arizona, with construction planned to complete in late 2028 to early 2029 for what could be the US’s next premier esports venue.
First announced all the way back in January 2020, Atari Hotels promises to bring a combination of cutting-edge technology, first-of-its-kind entertainment, and hospitality to guests in the United States, with its first project now underway.
As told in a press release shared with IGN, groundbreaking will commence this week in Phoenix’s Roosevelt Row. The hotel is expected to feature “high-tech guest rooms,” creator studios, and an esports and concert venue that can house more than two thousand attendees, along with a sportsbook, “layers of immersive bars,” shopping, “immersive experiences,” and restaurants.
Atari Hotel Concept Art (2026)
Currently, construction is in Phase One, which will demo the building currently on the property and begin work to lay the new hotel’s foundation. Phase Two will begin shortly after this is done. (Among its partners and celebrity investors is, oddly, FaZe Adapt, as well as American professional wrestler Henry Cejudo.)
“We’re pressing ‘start’ on Atari Hotels’ Phoenix property, bringing our vision for the first-of-its-kind venue closer to reality,” Jordan Taylor, a Partner at Intersection Development, said in a statement. “The opportunity to build an interactive venue like this in our hometown with an incredible partner like Atari is a privilege, and we’re excited to celebrate this milestone with the community as we break ground.”
“We’re excited to see construction begin on the Atari Hotel and believe in Intersection Development’s vision to create something that speaks to gaming as a consistent pillar of pop culture,” Wade Rosen, Chairman and CEO of Atari, added. “This project puts the Atari brand at the heart of a brand-new entertainment experience for fans, tourists, and Phoenix locals.”
Atari Hotel Concept Art
The Atari Hotel is being designed by räkkhaus, which describes itself as an “an avant-garde architecture studio that embodies the fusion of love, form, and revolution.” Given that it's licensed by Atari, the hotel will combine gaming and hospitality with hopes to “capitalize on the growing intersection of gaming, sports, entertainment, and pop culture.”
The first concept art for the property made its way online in October 2020, showing a Cyberpunk exterior that looked like something straight out of Night City. This planned version of the hotel was shaped like the Atari logo, with the artwork showing off futuristic statues of robots and bright neon lighting. Newer images paint a different picture, though, and one that looks more appropriate for this time period.
This is almost as neat as the two Dragon Ball theme parks that are planned to be built in France and Qiddiya City. Concept art for the first park, shared in 2024, shows a giant Shenron statue on an island in the middle of a massive pond, with other areas seemingly taken straight out of the show.
Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero is here and it’s taking over Steam’s most-played chart already, but there’s a day one patch that you should install before you play.
item.description:
Phantom Blade Zero is here and it’s taking over Steam’s most-played chart already, but there’s a day one patch that you should install before you play.
As well as fixing a slew of bugs, the patch offers performance advantages for PC and console players. It’s approximately 5GB in size on PC and 2GB on PS5 (on PS5 the patch appears as version 1.301.524).
The patch improves ray tracing and path tracing, making the real-time lighting and shadows pop even more, with rasterization (the process of converting 3D models to real-time) improvements “ensuring the scene’s art style is perfectly conveyed, even with ray tracing disabled.”
Phantom Blade Zero - Donnie Yen Behind the Scenes Photos
In other words, it should still look good on mid-range PCs and even handheld devices like the Steam Deck. Though the game is not yet Steam Deck Verified by Valve, developer S-Game said handheld devices have been “extensively tested,” so it’s likely verification is just around the corner.
For PC players, the developer said it had noticed some performance issues on the latest Nvidia drivers: 621.01. “We found that Nvidia’s latest driver 621.01 has some unstable performance issues,” S-Game said in the patch announcement.
The developer recommends rolling back to 617.42 for optimal performance, but Nvidia will likely roll out a new driver soon anyway.
Here's the detail of Phantom Blade Zero's day-one patch, from Soulframe LIANG, creative director and CEO of S-Game:
News broke earlier that the original Phantom Blade Zero protagonist actor had been replaced. Instead, Sonic the Hedgehog himself, Roger Craig Smith, takes the lead role for the full launch.
IGN's Phantom Blade Zero review returned a 9/10. We said: "Phantom Blade Zero is an unbelievably smooth action game filled with memorable boss fights, compelling combat, and limitless swagger."
Before you step into the Phantom World, we’ve put together a helpful list of Things Phantom Blade Zero Doesn’t Tell You. We’ve also got a step-by-step Phantom Blade Zero Walkthrough in progress, plus guides for the game’s Weapons, Accessories, and Phantom Edges.

item.title: Security experts have issued a warning over fake PS5 emulators after they found scammers were tricking gamers into downloading malware.
item.description:
Security experts have issued a warning over fake PS5 emulators after they found scammers were tricking gamers into downloading malware.
NordVPN's Threat Intelligence research team said it had identified a scam campaign that was spreading malware through GitHub repositories disguised as PS5 emulation software for PC.
The scammers are exploiting two well-known emulator projects to trick gamers into downloading what appears to be an infostealer. The malware uses heavy anti-analysis tricks to evade detection, adds itself to Windows Defender exclusions, and deletes its own traces after infection, NordVPN said.
The Best PS5 Games
The scam campaign is taking advantage of increasing interest in PS5 emulation on PC, which has exploded in recent months as hackers use AI to assist their efforts. PS5 exclusives such as Astro Bot and the Demon’s Souls Remake, for example, were recently shown running on PC.
"Emulation fans are a perfect target. They are used to downloading experimental software from GitHub and running unsigned files, so nothing about this feels suspicious," said Marijus Briedis, chief technology officer at NordVPN. "But this is not an emulator. It steals your data, hides from your antivirus, and erases its own tracks before you notice anything is wrong."
Last week, Sony issued a new PS5 firmware update that some believe was designed to combat the homebrew community's ongoing effort to jailbreak the console. There is a game of Whac-A-Mole at play where the homebrew scene is working to release a new jailbreak for the latest PS5 firmware, then do it all over again when Sony releases a new firmware update designed to beef up security.
This in turn has sparked concern that if a PS5 jailbreak is made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6, which comes out next month, then it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and maybe even made available on PC.
IGN reported on a hacker who had sparked an uproar within the PS5 homebrew scene for privately reporting an exploit to Sony and cashing in on a $50,000 reward, rather than keeping it confidential for the community.
Photographer: Kiyoshi Ota/Bloomberg via Getty Images.

item.title: In the trailers leading up to launch, Phantom Blade Zero protagonist Soul was voiced by up and coming actor Jay Maksenuk, best known for playing V in Once Human. As the game moved into release, however, he was replaced.
item.description:
In the trailers leading up to launch, Phantom Blade Zero protagonist Soul was voiced by up-and-coming actor Jay Maksenuk, best known for playing V in Once Human. As the game moved into release, however, he was replaced.
Now Roger Craig Smith — best known as Sonic the Hedgehog, Ezio Auditore, Batman, and Chris Redfield — plays the role. You can check out the new performance in the Phantom Blade Zero launch trailer below.
The actor is joined by Mu Xiaokui actor Maggie Robertson, who played Lady Dimitrescu in Resident Evil 7. Elsewhere in the cast, Donnie Yen served as a key creative consultant and stars as the character Mó Yuan (Soul's father) through full facial, voice, and motion capture.
Maksenuk originally posted about landing the role on Reddit and was listed as the game’s protagonist on IMDb. However, the Reddit post has since been deleted and IMDb no longer lists Phantom Blade Zero among the actor’s credits. IGN has asked Maksenuk and Smith for comment.
Phantom Blade Zero looks like a smash hit already. It's ahead of eternal Steam big hitters PUBG and Dota 2 by peak concurrent players on Valve's platform, and behind only Counter-Strike 2 as the most-played game. But it's worth noting that the total peak player count will be even higher, given Phantom Blade Zero is also out on PS5 (Sony does not make player numbers public). It's also the best-selling game on Steam by revenue, ahead of Activision Modern Warfare 4, Aion 2, and Probably Stolen, a Cyberpunk shopkeeper sim that's going viral.
IGN's Phantom Blade Zero review returned a 9/10. We said: "Phantom Blade Zero is an unbelievably smooth action game filled with memorable boss fights, compelling combat, and limitless swagger."
Before you step into the Phantom World, we’ve put together a helpful list of Things Phantom Blade Zero Doesn’t Tell You. We’ve also got a step-by-step Phantom Blade Zero Walkthrough in progress, plus guides for the game’s Weapons, Accessories, and Phantom Edges.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Arrowhead has switched to Easy Anti-Cheat to cut down on cheaters in Helldivers 2, but that decision has proven controversial on Steam. The new anti-cheat was supposed to prevent mods that give players unfair advantages, but it’s broken mods players use to tidy up the game.
item.description:
Arrowhead has switched to Easy Anti-Cheat to cut down on cheaters in Helldivers 2, but that decision has proven controversial on Steam. The new anti-cheat was supposed to prevent mods that give players unfair advantages, but it’s broken mods players use to tidy up the game.
"We know mods are part of the DNA of PC gaming and gaming communities as a whole," the studio wrote in a post last week. "In general, we appreciate the creativity behind cosmetic and non-gameplay mods, which players can enjoy without negatively impacting those who play alongside them.
"Where we need to improve is how we protect players against modifications that create unfair advantages or negatively impact others, which goes beyond software manipulation to tamper with our game."
Following the change, recent reviews on Steam plummeted to “Mostly Negative,” while all-time reviews of the game remain “Mostly Positive.” Many have called out Arrowhead for punishing players for using mods that fix, in their opinion, issues with the game the developer has failed to address.
Useful mods include hellpod steering fixes, smoother vaulting and climbing mechanics, AI improvements, and more. Easy Anti-Cheat doesn’t differentiate between these and, say, mods that give players invincibility.
Some players have claimed the anti-cheat blocked them from launching the game at all, despite no mod installs. Currently, in the UK, the game doesn’t even appear on Steam.
“Arrowhead could have embraced the mods,” one Steam review said. “There could have been Workshop support, Left 4 Dead 2 is still thriving to this day. Arrowhead could have had public vanilla lobbies separate from modded ones. Baldur’s Gate 3 has this!”
Helldivers 2 is a co-op game where players work together to fight off various alien races across the galaxy, as enemies fill the screen, bullets fly, and your squadmates die in horrible and hilarious ways. From Arrowhead’s perspective, mods could help you grind to unlock all those cosmetics you could otherwise pay real money for.
IGN has asked Arrowhead for comment.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: The boss of Xbox has insisted that sales of the console are constrained by supply and that there is “more demand than consoles available,” as Microsoft’s gaming business heads into the crucial holiday season.
item.description:
The boss of Xbox has insisted that sales of the console are constrained by supply and that there is “more demand than consoles available,” as Microsoft’s gaming business heads into the crucial holiday season.
Microsoft reported its FY27 Q1 results overnight, and the Xbox struggle is a familiar one despite new CEO Asha Sharma’s “reset” of the gaming business. During the three months ending September 30, 2026, overall Xbox revenue declined 2% year-on-year, although that’s an improvement on the 10% decline the previous quarter.
Xbox content and services revenue decreased 2% and 1% in constant currency, driven by “declines in third-party content and Xbox Game Pass, partially offset by growth in first-party content.” Xbox hardware sales, meanwhile, fell 14%. Xbox console sales, which have seen a number of price rises, have struggled for some time now, and Microsoft hasn't reported a sales figure for the Series X and S for years.
The 100 Best Xbox Games of All Time
Despite the financial struggles, Xbox is still a huge business. It brought in $5.379 billion in the quarter ($5.508 billion the same quarter last year). But Xbox is a small piece of the overall Microsoft pie. To put Xbox into context, Microsoft’s cloud computing platform, Azure, brought in an eye-watering $33.1 billion this quarter alone — six times more than Xbox.
It’s worth noting that the recently released Gears of War: E-Day and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 came after the end of Q1, so any revenue attributed to those games will be calculated in the current quarter’s results. Q2, by the way, also includes the likes of World of Warcraft: Forever, which looks like a surefire hit for Blizzard, and the behemoth that is Grand Theft Auto 6.
Sharma took to X / Twitter to discuss the results, insisting Xbox’s “accountability margin,” which is understood to be profit margin, improved this quarter. Sharma’s restructure of Xbox, which has seen thousands of staff lose their jobs, multiple studios leave the fold, and various projects shut down, was explained in the summer as part of an effort to improve this “accountability margin” figure. Xbox is now doubling down on its big hitters, such as Minecraft, Fallout, and The Elder Scrolls, in a bid to improve its financial outlook.
Minecraft and WoW Forever “set records,” (in the case of WoW Forever, we’re talking about the hugely popular beta). Neither Activision nor Microsoft has announced sales for Modern Warfare 4, instead pointing to the critical acclaim Infinity Ward’s shooter has enjoyed. “Call of Duty had its most acclaimed release in more than a decade,” Sharma said. PC platform revenue, though, grew “double digits” (we don’t know how much exactly, or what that means in dollar terms).
Every Video Game Franchise Xbox Owns After Acquiring Activision Blizzard
And then Sharma’s main point: “Console sales remain constrained by supply, with more demand than consoles available. We’re working to get more consoles into players’ hands, including through our expanded refurbishment program. We’re making progress, with a lot more work ahead.”
Last week, IGN reported on how Xbox was sending emails to customers reminding them that they could trade in their Series X and S consoles if they were collecting dust. The email was reportedly sent to customers in the U.S. who hadn’t used their console in some time.
The past year or so has seen console prices skyrocket thanks to the 'RAMpocalypse' sparked by generative AI companies such as OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Microsoft itself gobbling up components. As these AI companies vie for dominance and hoard all the RAM, prices soar for the end user while hardware is harder than ever to get hold of.

item.title: It’s only been out a few hours, but Phantom Blade Zero is already a big hit on Steam, topping the best-selling games chart, and reaching a huge peak concurrent player count of 448,000.
item.description:
It’s only been out a few hours, but Phantom Blade Zero is already a big hit on Steam, topping the best-selling games chart, and reaching a huge peak concurrent player count of 448,000.
Phantom Blade Zero is ahead of eternal Steam big hitters PUBG and Dota 2 by peak concurrent players, and behind only Counter-Strike 2 as the most-played game on Valve's platform. But it's worth noting that the total peak player count will be even higher, given Phantom Blade Zero is also out on PS5 (Sony does not make player numbers public).
It's also the best-selling game on Steam by revenue, ahead of Activision Modern Warfare 4, Aion 2, and Probably Stolen, a Cyberpunk shopkeeper sim that's going viral.
Phantom Blade Zero - Donnie Yen Behind the Scenes Photos
The early success shouldn't come as a huge surprise. This week, it was estimated that Phantom Blade Zero had sold over 1 million copies before launch, across launch platforms Steam and PS5, and Tencent’s WeGame (an online PC storefront in China). Nearly two thirds of total prelaunch sales were from China, Taiwan, or Hong Kong. Phantom Blade Zero is a wuxia action game developed by Chinese studio S-Game, and features martial arts movie star Donnie Yen.
Alongside the launch of the game, creative director and S-Game CEO, Soulframe Liang, penned a heartfelt letter thanking fans. In it, he talked about the game’s humble beginnings — a version of the world he created as a student in RPG Maker called Rainblood: Town of Death.
“Back then, I had no idea where my life or career would lead,” he said. “Making games had simply been a source of comfort while I studied abroad, but before I knew it, it had become one of the most important parts of my life.
“More than three years ago, when we brought our first, still rather rough Phantom Blade Zero trailer to a PlayStation showcase, we probably looked like a new studio being a little too bold, putting an unfinished game out for the whole world to judge. Phantom Blade was simply another original IP, its world, characters and story entirely unfamiliar to people.”
He went on to explain how the reaction to the trailer spurred the team on, and they cancelled other projects to focus on Phantom Blade while expanding the scale of production. They travelled across China to 3D scan villages, captured thousands of hours of motion capture, and went to Shaolin temples and sword masters to learn martial arts.
Soulframe also called out a few young and hungry developers on the team, such as art director Michael Chang, who drew concepts for every single character and environment. “After years of development, I feel that technology and experience have become the baseline, almost a given at this point,” he continued. “What I find myself paying more attention to now is the mindset of the people behind the game. Beyond skill and experience, is there a certain madness, a certain obsession?”
Soulframe explained that over time, the team started to feel like wuxia characters themselves, fighting battles each day to make the best game possible. “Over the past few years, one thing I often said to the team was, ‘Today, I have a suffocating decision to announce,’” he explained. “That usually meant taking apart something everyone had already carefully built and polished, then rebuilding it, or even abandoning it altogether.
“It meant a great deal of rework, and sometimes letting go of content that had already taken an enormous amount of time and effort. I am deeply grateful to the team for their understanding and support. We did it. We have poured all our thought and creativity into this game.”
He finished the post off by thanking players who followed the game’s journey from scrappy indie game to topping the Steam charts on its first day out.
IGN's Phantom Blade Zero review returned a 9/10. We said: "Phantom Blade Zero is an unbelievably smooth action game filled with memorable boss fights, compelling combat, and limitless swagger."
Before you step into the Phantom World, we’ve put together a helpful list of Things Phantom Blade Zero Doesn’t Tell You. We’ve also got a step-by-step Phantom Blade Zero Walkthrough in progress, plus guides for the game’s Weapons, Accessories, and Phantom Edges.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: GTA 6 made a surprise appearance on South Park with just shy of 20 seconds of genuine, exclusive gameplay that showcased dog poop.
item.description:
GTA 6 made a surprise appearance on South Park with just shy of 20 seconds of genuine, exclusive gameplay that showcased dog poop.
The latest episode of Trey Parker and Matt Stone’s hit comedy series, titled Guinea Pig On A Stick, shows a dog doing a poo on a beach (this is South Park after all!). The NPC dog walker picks up the poo, and here things get a little messy. We see Jason attack the NPC with the dog poo, which explodes in their face. That's one way to start a fight.
The gameplay is shown during a scene in which the main characters visit a cattle ranche, where a woman hypes up GTA 6 by providing a quick look at the game. “The graphics are seriously next level,” the woman says. “You see the worldbuilding? It’s a dog taking a poop. And people can pick up the dog poop. You can throw things at the person with dog poop, and if they choose to fight back, you can pick up the dog poop and actually attack them with the dog poop. That is what’s coming in November.”
“Wow!” Stan says. “Holy s**t!” Kyle exclaims. “Dude, that game looks f***ing tits!” Cartman offers.
Here’s the FULL GTA 6 gameplay footage exclusively shown in the latest South Park episode in HD. https://t.co/aMBXWtnKE3
The woman is voiced by Tish Hicks (as confirmed in the credits of the episode). Hicks is a voice actor who narrated the GTA 5 gameplay trailer all those years ago, so fans will probably find her voice familiar.
As for the gameplay, Rockstar had confirmed the dog poop mechanic already, but it’s fun to see it in action. And it’s great to get a sense of the density of NPCs on the beach in gameplay, too, given this sort of scene has been at the heart of official pre-launch videos and screenshots.
South Park is of course no stranger to video games, with its 2006 World of Warcraft episode perhaps the most high-profile example of Parker and Stone taking aim at the culture. But it’s also had plenty to say about Rockstar games, too. Red Dead Redemption 2, for example, was at the heart of episodes Time to Get Cereal and Nobody Got Cereal?, which featured the game heavily.
In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023
With GTA 6’s November 19 release date just weeks away, Rockstar’s marketing has ramped up considerably. And we’re learning more and more about how the game works every day. Overnight, we learned how GTA 6 named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme, and how GTA 6's map will open up relatively early and let you explore freely.

item.title: GTA 6 has named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme.
item.description:
GTA 6 has named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme.
In 2008, a Justin.tv channel (now known as Twitch) by the name of FourPlayerPodcast made GTA history. One of the hosts of the channel, Brad Simons, rode a moped around GTA 4's Liberty City. He eventually found another moped rider and began comically declaring them "scooter brothers." The video has over 7.5 million views on YouTube, and now it's part of GTA 6.
In a new preview from Edge magazine, it was confirmed that players will be able to summon their vehicle using an app called Scooter Brothers. An NPC will deliver your car and then get on a scooter (presumably driven by another "brother") and drive off. Whether or not these so-called scooter brothers will have their own silly lines to honor their origins remains to be seen.
GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN
In GTA 5, when switching to Trevor, players would have a chance of seeing the wily character recreating the meme with a frightened NPC. It was a pretty great nod, and now, Rockstar is keeping the tradition alive, though this time with more purpose.
GTA Online has had a mechanic to let you call your car since launch, and Red Dead Redemption also allows you to summon your horse if it's within a reasonable distance. However, this is the first time players will be able to do something like this without cheats in GTA's single-player. It's arguably more necessary than ever, too, as the player's arsenal of weapons and some other important gear is stored in the trunk of their vehicle. It also means your cars likely won't be as disposable as they were in previous games.
All of this news comes just three weeks ahead of GTA 6's launch and two weeks before pre-loading begins. Rockstar's marketing efforts are ramping up across the globe. Rumors also indicate a PC version of the game is just around the corner, with a reported release window of early 2027. Either way, it's an exciting time to be a GTA fan.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: GTA 6's world won't be blocked off by story progression, Rockstar confirms.
item.description:
GTA 6's world won't be blocked off by story progression, Rockstar confirms.
In a new preview from Edge magazine (as relayed by the podcast GTA VI O'Clock), Rockstar Games confirmed a ton of new details about GTA 6. One of the big bits revealed was that GTA 6's map will open up relatively early. In some GTA games, like GTA 4, the game forces you to progress through its story before you can access the entire map. GTA 4's Liberty City uses police blockades on bridges to make sure the world only expands as Niko continues his journey. That changed in GTA 5, as you could go wherever your heart desired once the game's tutorials were finished.
It seems like GTA 6 will be similar, as Edge's story confirms that the state of Leonida will open up relatively early on. Of course, there will likely be some initial story bits to introduce the characters and mechanics before you can go wherever you want. So, if you wish to head north and see the top of the map at the start of the game, you can do so. Of course, the story itself will take you to a lot of places around the map as you experience it, but you won't be chained to Vice City for the first 10 hours if you don't want to be.
Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games
Red Dead Redemption 2 also largely lets the player freely explore the map, but there was one area that they couldn't visit until the end of the game: the entire map from the first Red Dead Redemption. While there wasn't as much to see and do there, it was a fun surprise that almost doubled the scope of the game's map. If players tried to go there before the story was ready, they would be shot and killed by snipers.
Similarly, the first Red Dead Redemption game prevented the player from visiting Mexico until John Marston's journey took him there. It seems like GTA 6 will give players a lot of freedom off the bat... and it may take a while before you see anything. Rockstar North co-studio head Aaron Garbut also confirmed that he's still discovering new locations in Leonida.
Part of that comes from how dense the game is, with Garbut noting that there are "an order of magnitude more interiors" compared to other Rockstar titles, and all of them have been handcrafted with an exceptional level of detail.
GTA 6 will release on November 19 for Xbox Series X|S and PS5.

item.title: BioWare co-founder Greg Zeschuk has spoken out about the closure of BioWare last week, which saw 50 jobs lost as part of 400 cuts across the company, along with the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, which we've now come to learn (via a leaked internal trailer) was called Mass Effect: Universe.
item.description:
BioWare co-founder Greg Zeschuk has spoken out about the closure of BioWare last week, which saw 50 jobs lost as part of 400 cuts across the company, along with the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, which we've now come to learn (via a leaked internal trailer) was called Mass Effect: Universe.
Speaking to 80 Level, Zeschuk lamented the end of the studio but said he went through his own emotional goodbye to the studio after he and fellow co-founder Ray Muzyka departed it on their own terms back in 2012, several months after the launch of Mass Effect 3. “I've kind of gone through all the emotions like long, long ago,” he said. “You have to break from it and kind of go, ‘OK, I've had my emotional moment.’” He continued: “I'm just at a point in my life where I've got my own other business,” he said. “My [beer] brewing business is going really well. I've got a whole other thing I'm doing, and I'm not sentimental or nostalgic. I'm kind of, like, that chapter's closed.”
That said, he certainly had opinions regarding the closure of the great RPG studio he helped build. “I’m not saying it doesn’t hurt and doesn’t suck," he said. "And I think it’s kind of sad. It’s actually, in some ways, saddest for the city of Edmonton, where we’re from, because we were kind of this beacon of hope and excitement and possibility. We showed you could do something really special in a place that was not known for doing things like that.”
Regarding the Saudi Public Investment Fund's $55 private buyout of EA, Zeschuk said he wasn't surprised that BioWare was ultimately shut down. “I think it was the final nail in the coffin,” he said. “I think that was the crux of it in a sense. Once again it's a completely different company now... BioWare makes these kind of unusual games that take a long time and they're complicated and so it's easier just to pump out sports games every year and that's a better business model in some ways.”
Zeschuk wasn't shy about his feelings on executives without any game-development experience owning and running game development studios.
“There’s this weird belief that you can just kind of recreate great games with random people and AI. It doesn’t work,” he proclaimed. “The other harsh reality of almost all these companies, the people that go down the business track never really come from the development track. Because none of these people have ever made a game, like, never really sat and made one, like, from start to finish, even a small thing, they just don’t know how it works.”
Public reactions to the closure of BioWare and cancellation of Mass Effect have been strong. Here at IGN, I wrote about how BioWare was the greatest RPG developer ever, Jackie Thomas lamented that BioWare will never get the chance to redeem itself after Mass Effect Andromeda, and Matt Purslow wrote that EA never really knew what it had with BioWare. Meanwhile, composer Austin Wintory revealed he'd been in discussions with EA and BioWare about composing the soundtrack for Mass Effect 5 and was such a fan of the series that he even went so far as to release 22 minutes of Mass Effect music he'd created to help convince the publisher to hire him. And in the wider gaming public, fans expressed anger and sadness at the loss of a studio with such an incredible legacy.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: A 1981 promotional poster for the original Donkey Kong, featuring the first public appearance of Mario, has become the the most expensive piece of original video game art ever sold at auction.
item.description:
A 1981 promotional poster for the original Donkey Kong, featuring the first public appearance of Mario, has become the the most expensive piece of original video game art ever sold at auction.
But this artwork nearly got thrown out in the garbage. According to Landry Pop Auctions, who facilitated the sale, a former Nintendo of America employee named Donna Darbous saved the poster from a collection of materials that were marked for disposal.
The poster was drawn by artist Leslie Cabarga as an arcade flyer for Nintendo of America, depicting Donkey Kong angrily hoisting a barrel over his head as a determined Mario — then simply named ‘Jumpman’ — makes his way up a building to save Pauline, who cowers in fear behind her hulking captor.
As told in a press release shared with IGN, this flyer has now sold for an eye-watering $329,400, making it the most expensive video game artwork ever sold at auction. That record was previously held by the original cover artwork for Prince of Persia, which sold at Heritage Auctions in 2023 for $63,000 — meaning the Donkey Kong poster blew it out of the water by a staggering $266,400.
The poster inspired a sale of other historic Nintendo artworks titled Landry Pop Auctions' Jumpman: The Beginning of an Icon. This event included original production artwork from Super Mario Bros. and even some of the first illustrations of the game series’ iconic enemies.
For example, original artwork of Mario and Luigi from Super Mario Bros. sold for $17,080, which Landry Pop Auctions said was nearly three times its estimate of $6,000. Original artwork of a Goomba, an ever-recurring enemy in the Mario games, raked in $10,370, more than double its $5,000 estimate.
Landry Pop Auctions' Jumpman: The Beginning of an Icon Images
A first-production 1985 copy of Super Mario Bros. for the NES , boasting an 8.0 grading from PSA, went for $34,160, while a curious piece of history, a Nintendo of America employee orientation VHS tape that featured Mario, was also sold in this auction for $3,660 against its $1,500 estimate.
"Long before Mario became the face of a multibillion-dollar entertainment franchise, he was a character on an arcade flyer. The $329,400 result is a striking reminder of how far Nintendo's most famous plumber has come, and how valuable the surviving artwork from his earliest days has become," Landry Pop Auctions said in a press release.
This is the latest game-related auction sale to raise eyebrows after a retired decorator in the UK sold their collection of Pokemon cards for $2 million earlier this month. And in June, a PSA-graded 9.6 A++ copy of Super Mario Bros. for the NES was sold at auction for a record-breaking $3 million, becoming the most expensive video game in history.
Image Credits: Nintendo of America, Landry Pop Auctions

item.title: Backrooms director Kane Parsons has confirmed he has had meetings with Valve, but he has no plans to adapt any of their IP if it can't be done well.
item.description:
Backrooms director Kane Parsons has confirmed his meetings with Valve, but says that he has no plans to adapt any of their games if it can't be done well.
When speaking on an October 28 episode of The Kyle Buchanan Show, Parsons wore a Valve hoodie, which prompted Buchanan to inquire about Parsons' recent trips to the developer's corporate offices. (Following the release of Backrooms, the director noted that he wanted to make a Portal movie and subsequently posted about trips to Valve on Instagram.) Naturally, Parsons didn't confirm or deny what exactly is going on between them, but confirmed that he has had conversations with the company — but he only wants to work with them if it's done right.
"They work in experiments, and I like that, because that tends to be how I work," he said. "I don't have a desire to sensationalize anything I may or may not be talking to them about over there, because it's mainly: Is it possible to make something compelling in some way that we like? What do you guys want to do? What do I want to do? Is there anything on the table in any way, shape, or form?
Portal: Companion Collection Screenshots
"And if it's not, I would defend a future where we don't even go down that road, but it's more like having an abstract creative conversation that could flow in like 30 different directions. If you know the way Valve works, I think they're looking to experiment more internally than anything that's going to be talked about. If something cool comes of it, I am sure somehow, people will know."
As noted, Parsons has expressed interest in making a Portal movie and also recently confirmed that he is working on three "dream projects." These projects seem to be linked to some kind of IP, but Parsons has also previously stated he has no real interest in a property like Star Wars, and his desire for adaptations lies more within a small handful of things from his childhood, such as Valve's games.
Whether a Portal movie actually happens remains to be seen, but it's good to hear that Parsons isn't simply trying to jack the franchise from Valve. Although there hasn't been a new mainline Portal game since 2011, interest in the series remains high among fans. Perhaps a film could inspire a new game... or maybe Parsons has ambitions beyond a movie and would like to do something with the game's developers, instead. He has extensive experience with Blender, so he isn't out of his element, after all.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: James Gunn has clarified DC Studios’ 8-10 year roadmap and confirmed its focus on Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman as its “diamond characters.”
item.description:
James Gunn has clarified DC Studios’ 8-10 year roadmap and confirmed its focus on Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman as its “diamond characters.”
Gunn shared this information on Threads in response to a now-deleted post, where he urged the original poster to study up on his quotes from January 2023 in regards to what his version of the DCU will end up looking like.
“I said some stories would be standalone like the Guardians movies were (which is what Clayface is), and some stories would have part of a larger narrative structure, which is what the Superman Saga is. All that said, each piece of the larger story should work on its own with or without having to see everything else,” he said.
Ranking the Superman Actors
He went on to clarify that the “often-cited 8-10 year roadmap” for the DCU doesn’t just apply to story points, but also outlines the plan for “DC as a whole.” This includes focusing on “diamond characters,” which Gunn confirmed are, perhaps unsurprisingly, Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman, as well as “smaller characters we could turn into diamonds.” These smaller characters were listed as Krypto the Superdog, John Stewart, and Peacemaker.
According to Gunn, this plan also factors in how DC will “foster filmmaker freedom and allow for multiple tones and ratings, the influences of Star Wars and George R.R. Martin, and so much more."
“It's exciting seeing things start to come together, and all that makes me even more excited for what we have in store for everyone in Man of Tomorrow,” he said.
It’s encouraging to see Gunn confirm that Batman and Wonder Woman are still a big focus for his DCU, given that we haven’t seen hide nor hair of Wonder Woman and barely a glimpse of Batman’s silhouette in the animated Creature Commandos series.
Thus far, the only “diamond character” mentioned in this specific post that has been featured in Gunn’s DCU is Superman. Elsewhere, the Lanterns and Clayface have finally gotten some love (with Lanterns receiving rave reviews, though audience opinions on Clayface have been a mixed bag), and The People v. Gorilla Grodd is also in the works. It seems that Supergirl wasn’t mentioned as either a “diamond character” or a character that could be turned "into a diamond" in Gunn's post — though, given that she had her own movie, it’s safe to assume that she has firmly established her place in the DCU hierarchy as a central figure.
Batman is another story altogether. Unrelated to Matt Reeves’ The Batman movies, the DCU’s take on the caped crusader has yet to be revealed; while Alan Ritchson was a popular pick from fans, DC Studios boss Peter Safran has stated they still haven’t found the right role for him to play. Batman is set to have his own movie in the DCU, titled The Brave and the Bold, which is in the works but has no official release date.
Where Wonder Woman fits in Gunn’s DCU is just as nebulous. Similarly, no casting has been confirmed for this part, though fans are convinced that Adria Arjona will soon wield the Lasso of Truth on screen. It’s also unclear when, or how, she’ll be introduced to things, but Gunn has made it clear that she’s a priority.
In other exciting DC news, a live-action Poison Ivy show was confirmed to be in the works earlier this month, with The Penguin showrunner Lauren LeFranc set to produce. Similarly, no casting has been confirmed (though rumors of ScarJo playing the character continue to swirl).

item.title: During a recent appearance at a book festival, Outlander star Sam Heughan strongly suggested that he may have a role in the upcoming film The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum.
item.description:
Outlander star Sam Heughan has strongly suggested that he may have a role in the upcoming film The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum.
Heughan spoke earlier this month at Scotland’s Wigtown Book Festival, during which the topic of J. R. R. Tolkien’s literary saga and subsequent film adaptations came up.
This wouldn’t be an unusual topic to raise with Heughan, as he’s named after Samwise Gamgee and his brother, Cirdan, is named after an Elf. (Their parents belonged to a London hippie community called Gandalf's Garden.)
When the moderator suggested the Lord of the Rings film franchise was “exhausted” at this point, Heughan cryptically replied, "No, it's not exhausted. I'm not giving anything away, but I may have been in New Zealand recently." You can watch the exchange for yourself below.
Sam Heughan on The Hunt for Gollum https://t.co/EeVmIaxx3l
The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum has been filming in New Zealand under the direction of Andy Serkis.
And as Winter Is Coming points out, “another eagle-eyed Outlander fan account, @samjamie_stillhere, noticed that a rare edition of The Letters of J.R.R. Tolkien went up for auction to benefit the ALS Network, which was signed by ‘people who have taken his world to the screen, and people who are taking it there next.’ The list of signatures includes a number of stars and producers from The Hunt for Gollum, all of whom have their roles for the film listed... as well as Sam Heughan.”
Maybe Heughan was just visiting the set of The Hunt for Gollum as a fan, or perhaps he has a heretofore undisclosed role in the film. If so, who do you think he plays? Let us know in the comments.
For more coverage on all things Middle-earth, read why Jamie Dornan isn’t trying to “outdo” Viggo Mortensen's Aragorn in The Hunt for Gollum and discover why The Rings of Power Season 3 is “turning the page on the show.”
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

item.title: The stars behind GTA 5’s Franklin, Michael, and Trevor, along with the voice of CJ from San Andreas, were asked if they had any advice for the actors playing GTA 6’s Jason and Lucia now that the game is almost here.
item.description:
The stars behind GTA 5’s Franklin, Michael, and Trevor, along with the voice of CJ from San Andreas, were asked if they had any advice for the actors playing GTA 6’s Jason and Lucia now that the game is almost here.
The long wait for GTA 6 is almost over. After 13 years, the game is finally set to release on November 19 in one of the biggest (and potentially most expensive) pop culture moments in history.
Knowing just how passionate Rockstar’s fanbase can be, actors who starred in previous games in the franchise shared their words of wisdom with the as-yet unannounced actors who are playing Jason and Lucia, the dual protagonists of GTA 6, in an interview with All Out Gaming at MCM Comic Con.
GTA 6 Launch Trailer Screenshots
“Have fun,” CJ’s actor, Young Maylay, said.
“To be honest, just listen to what Rockstar says,” Shawn ‘Solo’ Fonteno, famous for playing Franklin in GTA 5, added. “They’re gonna lead you in the right direction. … But get ready. That’s all I can say, is get ready. It’s a ride that they’re gonna be on for a while.”
Young Maylay continued, remarking on how the GTA games have garnered dedicated fanbases from multiple generations of players. “We’ll always be the characters that we are, and for the generation of kids who are coming up, you’re gonna have certain brackets,” he said.
“Right now, I got all the OGs. Everybody coming in my line — you catch some youngsters, but you got guys with the grey hair coming in saying, ‘Hey man! You’re the guy, CJ!’ And they [gesturing to the GTA 5 cast] have all the youngsters right now. So, during this time period, you’re gonna grow with your fanbase. It’s not like everything’s gonna get shut down by you guys [speaking of GTA 6]… we’ll always be those characters, and you can’t take that from us.”
Ned Luke, who played Michael De Santa in GTA 5, urged the upcoming stars to be grateful for the game’s fans. “Just make sure that you appreciate the fans. Let the fans know… fake appreciation, they can smell it. You have to really appreciate them, genuinely, because what we have is because of them. If you don’t have the fans, you don’t got nothin’. They’re the game, and that’s the bottom line,” he imparted.
The cast's warm sentiments toward GTA fans is at odds with one particular star in the franchise: Steven Ogg, who infamously said he felt "nothing inside" regarding GTA 6 because he's "not a gamer" and has "never played a video game" before. That being said, he did suggest killing off his character at the beginning of GTA 6 as a means of "passing the torch" to the next era. "I think that would be cool, because it also acknowledges the fans of like, 'Hey, thank you.' Pass the torch, stomp Trevor's head in, and sort of put an end to that and allow a new generation to take over," he mused back in 2025.
Thus far, the actors who play Jason and Lucia have not been officially announced, though fans are extremely convinced that they’ve discovered the gal who lent her facial features to Jason’s partner in crime. Fans suspect she will be played by an actress named Manni L. Perez, as she has the exact same voice and bears a strong resemblance with the GTA protagonist. (For her part, she’s been very careful to honor her supposed NDA, if she really is involved in the project.)
The fervor around GTA 6 is at an all-time high. Rockstar is ramping up marketing for the title in a major way with a Vice City-themed takeover of Miami that includes massive signs advertising the fictional city, even partnering with the Miami Heat to give the team some Vice City uniforms for their November 18 game against the Milwaukee Bucks. Players will even get a chance to eat at one of the game’s fast food joints, Burger Shot, at the Kaseya Center while they watch the two teams face off on the court.

item.title: NFL fans expressed some pretty heated responses on social media to the first clip of Nicolas Cage in the upcoming movie Madden, where the Oscar winner portrays the legendary football TV commentator John Madden.
item.description:
NFL fans expressed some pretty heated responses on social media to the first clip of Nicolas Cage in the upcoming movie Madden, where the Oscar winner portrays the legendary football TV commentator John Madden.
Director David O. Russell’s film chronicles Madden’s relationship with Al Davis (played by Christian Bale) and Madden’s journey, as the official synopsis puts it, "from a Super Bowl-winning partnership with the Raiders, to becoming football’s most recognizable voice, to building the worldwide Madden NFL video game."
In the clip (seen below), Cage’s Madden sits opposite ​​Joel Murray’s Pat Summerall as Madden breaks down a play on the telestrator while the crew in the booth react to it.
And football commentary was never the same. #MaddenMovie. November 18. https://t.co/ywUVTnYtkf
Judging by the visceral responses from a slew of football fans on social media, they appear to be mostly upset that Cage doesn’t sound like the iconic sports host. (I guess these fans must have missed the film’s trailer, since this isn’t the first time Cage’s Madden performance has been revealed.)
Here's a sample of the kinds of responses that have been posted:
“This is a disgraceful portrayal of a great man.” – AFL Godfather
“What a nightmare. Madden was a Legendary coach - capital Legendary - and this is what they come up with?” – tonmile trader
“Sigh....this could have been so good. I can't not hear Cage's voice. Or not see Cage's face. This is an insulting caricature of John Madden. I don't know how this got made.” – Matthew Ross
“Nicolas Cage told the director of the new Madden movie that John Madden's voice 'may not be anatomically possible/ for him to do. They went ahead and made the whole movie anyway.” – Aakash Gupta
“I was wondering how Nicolas Cage was going to pull off being Madden. Turns out he didn’t pull it off at all.” – Brian O’Leary
“I mean this is basically a desecration of Madden’s legacy. Astoundingly bad.” – Mark Valorian
“He sounds like 10% Jimmy Stewart, 90% Nicolas Cage. 0% Madden.” – Edward Fear
“Everyone is rightfully dogpiling on Nicolas Cage as Madden here, but the Pat Summerall is even more disrespectful. Looks and sounds nothing like Pat, acts annoyed by Madden, seems to have no football knowledge of his own. This movie needs to be shelved.” – Tim Roberts
“There are going to have to be arrests. Accountability for this is a must.” – Rob Slater
Criticisms weren’t reserved just for the performances. Cinema Tweets blasted the man behind the camera in their post, saying, “David O. Russell might never direct a film again after Madden. Do I want that to happen? Of course not. I want Madden to be a huge success. But if this film turns out as bad as it looks (and based on this trailer…it looks bad), who would ever bankroll O. Russell again? He just made the worst film of his career with Amsterdam & if he follows it up with another flop, why would anyone take another chance on him? Especially when you consider how difficult he is to work with as a director. There’s a lot on the line for O. Russell right now.”
In addition to Cage and Bale, Madden also stars Kathryn Hahn, Sienna Miller, John Mulaney, and Shane Gillis. Madden opens in select theaters on November 18, 2026 via Amazon MGM Studios.
What did you think of Nicolas Cage's performance as John Madden based on that clip? Vote in the poll below.

item.title: Wendy’s — yes, the American fast food chain — is releasing a surprisingly gorgeous, pixelated, turn-based RPG on Steam, and the internet is legitimately stunned by how good it looks.
item.description:
Wendy’s — yes, the American fast food chain — is releasing a surprisingly gorgeous, pixelated, turn-based RPG on Steam, and the internet is legitimately stunned by how good it looks.
The game, titled WendyQuest: Legend of the Four Corner Stones, is a 2D RPG where players join Wendy in her journey to “battle evil mech-monsters to save a culinary kingdom in peril.”
A trailer and screenshots for the game show Wendy and a party of three other adventurers traversing terrain fraught with food-themed obstacles and duking it out with sentient menu items. For instance, one of the enemies Wendy faces is a container full of french fries that have transformed into snake-like monsters called ‘Frydusa.’ In one gameplay still, she must find a way around a river of sauce that has spilled out from a container.
WendyQuest: Legend of the Four Corner Stones Screenshots
The game’s dialogue seems to poke fun at itself, with Wendy saying in one screenshot, “Looks like he’s been writing notes to some guy named Baconator. No way that’s a real name.” In another, she asks, “Where’s the beef?”
Of course, Wendy can use a Dave’s Single, Junior Bacon Cheeseburger, and other menu items to restore her HP during battle, where she’s joined by allies like Sir Chicken and more.
The game is set to release “soon,” with no specific launch date given. It does have an official Steam page, suggesting that this isn’t just a gimmick game but an actual, fully-fledged title with real effort and intent behind it.
WendyQuest is developed by 81monkeys, an independent game studio based out of Port Moody, British Columbia. They are also working on a game called World of Anterra, which is described as “an innovative open world roleplaying game” inspired by “classic and modern” titles.
Thus far, reactions to Wendy’s pixelated project have been largely positive. “GOTY contender. This actually looks great,” one user joked on Twitter/X.
“Wait, why does it look kind of good?” another asked.
“I honestly miss fast food games....Excited to play this!” said another.
Still others are pleased that no AI was used in this game’s production, despite it being, for all intents and purposes, a marketing tactic. Its Steam page proudly states that the title is “100% fresh and 100% human made.”
Of course, others couldn’t help but compare it to Burger King’s infamous Sneak King game from ages long past (2006), where players could “step into the King’s royal shoes and use cunning stealth to sneak up behind unsuspecting people and bestow them with a delicious meal.” (While a novelty, it wasn't an especially 'good' game. We rated it a 6.7 out of 10.)
This isn't the first time Wendy's has made a game; in fact, it released a free, 100-page tabletop RPG back in 2019 called Feast of Legends where players could battle Ronald McDonald. I have to admit that the chain's latest game is one of the more ambitious fast food marketing tactics I’ve seen thus far, and oddly, I’m actually keen on playing it when it actually comes out. Dangit — now I’m craving a Frosty.

item.title: IGN can exclusively reveal the first trailer for Winnie-the-Pooh: Blood and Honey 3, which director Scott Chambers calls “absolute carnage.” The slasher sequel will open in late January 2027.
item.description:
IGN can exclusively reveal the first trailer for Winnie-the-Pooh: Blood and Honey 3, which director Scott Chambers calls “absolute carnage.” You can watch the new trailer via the player above or the embed below. The film’s teaser poster can also be seen below.
“After the brutal capture of Pooh, Tigger, and Rabbit by the sinister Woozles Circus, fifteen years pass and the once-feral creatures are transformed into attractions in a twisted traveling carnival run by the mysterious Karna, occult showman Shandor, and the immortal ringmaster Balthazar. Meanwhile, Momo Milne, an orphan desperate to uncover the truth about her missing mother, traces her last known whereabouts to Woozles Ltd. Alongside her outspoken best friend Billie, Momo infiltrates the circus by taking a job among its bizarre performers,” according to the official synopsis.
“As the girls uncover horrifying secrets behind the spectacle—including drugged half-human creatures, disappearances, and gruesome killings hidden behind the carnival lights—Momo realizes her mother’s disappearance is tied to the circus’ darkest mystery. Drawn into a nightmare where fairy tales become blood-soaked reality, Momo must survive Pooh and his monstrous companions while uncovering the truth before she becomes the next act in Woozles’ deadly show.”
The film is scripted by Richard Stanley (Color Out of Space, Dust Devil, Hardware).
In a statement provided to IGN, director Scott Chambers says “Winnie-the-Pooh: Blood and Honey 3 is absolute carnage. I counted 20 character deaths during filming, and every one of them was captured practically on camera using real prosthetics, special-effects makeup and physical gore effects. I think this is a thrilling new entry in the Blood and Honey universe. It is bigger, bloodier and more ambitious, but it also plays an important part in the wider story we are building. This film leads directly towards Poohniverse: Monsters Assemble—our Avengers-style crossover—and acts as a major stepping stone towards that eventual finale.”
Chambers continued, “The story reveals how these creatures became so angry, damaged and vengeful, giving audiences a deeper understanding of the monsters they have become. It also brings an exciting new character to life in Rabbit, voiced by the legendary Roger L. Jackson from Scream. His performance gives Rabbit a genuinely chilling presence, and I cannot wait for audiences to meet him.”
In addition to Jackson, Chambers and Stanley are also in the cast, with Stanley playing Balthazar Von Woozle. The cast also includes Josephine Blazier, Kira Reed, Leo Harris, Zena Donnelly, and Harrison Davis.
Furthermore, Winnie-the-Pooh: Blood and Honey 3 features prominent social media horror content creators Cris Parker (3C Films) and Slashertalk.
The film is from Jagged Edge Productions and will be distributed by ITN Distribution in late January 2027. Stuart Alson, Nicole Holland, and Evgeny Lensky serve as Executive Producers.
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

item.title: PlayStation is bringing back the '90s transparent trend with the Prism Collection, a spread of DualSense controllers and matching PS5 covers in three new colorways.
item.description:
PlayStation is bringing back the '90s transparent trend with the Prism Collection, a spread of DualSense controllers and matching PS5 covers in three new colorways.
Preorders open on November 10 at 10am local time ahead of the collection's full launch next year. The Prism Collection DualSense controllers, available in Flare Orange, Emerald Green, and Graphite Gray, are releasing globally with a recommended retail price (RRP) of $84.99 USD (€84.99/£74.99). Matching PS5 console covers have an RRP of $74.99 USD (€74.99/£64.99).
A PlayStation blog post offers a closer look at the new see-through designs. The images are accompanied by insights from the design team, who were particularly “excited to bring a transparent appearance to PS5.”
PlayStation Prism Collection DualSense Controllers
"We wanted to bring back the iconic see-through trend of the late '90s in a fresh, modern way that complements the PS5’s industrial design," said PlayStation designer Leo Cardoso. The blog post also highlights that the see-through casing offers a “closer look at the design and craftsmanship behind our DualSense controllers and PlayStation 5 consoles.”
Fellow designer Satoshi Aoyagi describes the three colors the team chose to showcase the transparent mould: “A vibrant orange that subtly takes on a rosy hue where the transparent material overlaps, a deep hunter green that gains depth through its transparency, and a cool-toned storm gray.”
The full Prism Collection will be available to preorder from PlayStation Direct and select retailers starting November 10, with the full release scheduled for February 4.
Sony has released over a dozen DualSense color variants in the PS5 generation on top of limited-edition controllers tied to specific game releases like Astro Bot and Death Stranding.
While the company is expanding the reach of its hardware collaborations, like a new DualSense controller with Kpop star Lisa, its most popular release of late was the 30th Anniversary PlayStation collection. With the Prism Collection, the design team appears to be doubling down on audience demand for retro designs that tap into nostalgia for classic gaming eras.
PlayStation as a whole continues to be embroiled in controversies stemming from Sony's decision to cut disc production as well as a number of studio closures. Despite the backlash, Sony saw a 22% increase in PS5 sales during the past month, likely tied to the release of Insomniac’s Wolverine and the lead-up to GTA 6.
Phantom Blade Zero is the next (sort of) PlayStation exclusive set to hit consoles, and according to our reviewer, it’s looking pretty darn good.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.
